Exercise A

Neutral or too blunt?

A neutral email is polite but not stiff. Use Dear, Could you…?, I was wondering if… and Kind regards. Avoid slang and orders, and avoid very formal, old-fashioned words. Choose the best option for each gap.

Before you start — optional, not marked
This is just to get you thinking. You can leave it empty and it does not count towards your score.
Part 1: An email to a lecturer

1 Dr Hall,

I am writing 2 you about booking a seminar room for our group. Could you 3 me how students book one?

I was wondering 4 you could suggest a time for a short meeting. Would it be possible 5 on Thursday afternoon?

Thank you 6 advance.

Part 2: Choose the best sentence

7. To the library office, about noise: 7

8. To a lecturer, about a deadline: 8

9. To a landlord, about the heating: 9

10. To the cafeteria office, about waste: 10

11. A reminder to a lecturer: 11

12. The ending of an email to a landlord: 12

Exercise B

Make it polite

Work with a partner in your breakout room, 10 minutes. Rewrite each blunt message as one or two neutral, polite sentences. Use at least three different phrases from Exercise A. Then type your versions here.

Keep the message, but change the tone. Do not make it longer than two sentences.

Exercise C

Your own request

Choose a real or realistic situation. Write a short request as it would appear in an email, after the greeting. Then read your partner's request aloud and reply to it.

Word count: 0 (aim for 40–60)

Say why you are writing, ask for one thing and say thank you. Do not use a command.
